title: Unlocking Developer Productivity across CPU and GPU with MAX: Chris Lattner
talk_summary: Chris Lattner pitches Modular's MAX framework and Mojo language as a unified inference stack replacing fragmented vendor libraries, claiming 5x speedups over llama.cpp on CPU and matching/beating cuBLAS on GPU matmul. It is a vendor/product keynote about self-hosting inference, not about agent orchestration, review, or developer workflow.

takeaways.technique: Self-hosted inference to escape per-token endpoint costs
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues that when inference endpoints are expensive or data must stay in-house, teams should run models on their own hardware via a unified framework rather than paying per-unit API costs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the inference end points are expensive and so sometimes you want to save money
takeaways.numbers: claims INT4/INT8 quantization 5x faster than llama.cpp on cloud CPUs

takeaways.technique: Quantized small-model serving for cheap tiers
takeaways.what_they_do: Ships generalizable INT4/INT6 quantization so a single familiar model runs fast on commodity CPUs, positioning it as a cheap inference tier.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we just shipped a release that has our in4 in6 K fancy quantization approach
takeaways.numbers: 5x faster than llama.cpp on cloud CPUs
